## Design

### 2026-11-03: I spent quite some time researching the whole thing, if it was even feasible, what were the connections going to be to connect each board to each other, and how do I make it so that the ESP32 can get

**2h**

I spent quite some time researching the whole thing, if it was even feasible, what were the connections going to be to connect each board to each other, and how do I make it so that the ESP32 can get 5 potentiometer's signals and move an arm with that. The research took a while and at least I got it mostly sorted out. Then I started making the schematic a bit. It's a mess now but I might organize it better and fully finish it, assign footprints, and then route it and finish up the settings soon. It's going pretty good so far though.

### 2026-11-03: I spent a really long time working on the PCB. I fully finished the schematics now and the wiring looks a bit funny but I didn't wanna have to put net labels on every single thing and wanted to try ju

**5h**

I spent a really long time working on the PCB. I fully finished the schematics now and the wiring looks a bit funny but I didn't wanna have to put net labels on every single thing and wanted to try just wiring it once. When it connected 2 wires it was annoying but overall it is way more fun than just putting net labels. I also tried adding a battery circuit to this but I don't think it came out the best...  I also added some diodes and other safety features and a ton of more capacitors and resistors. Doing halflife has really taught me well on all the electronic parts, taught me how to make pcbs, and is letting me make them so I can really use it, for free. The biggest reason why I couldn't do this was the budget to build everything but now with this I can truly make whatever I want. I also organized and routed the whole PCB. I'm probably going to add a few more features and might swap out the microcontroller as the current one is not up to my standards but it should suffice. Also, I don't know why I spaced the components so far apart in the schematics. I also need to double check if I adjusted the wire thickness and if I need to add a gnd fill zone.

### 2026-11-08: I contemplated a ton and came to the eventual realization that I wanted a new robotic arm so as a result, I'm making a massive motor controller. It takes some inspiration from the first design and fir

**5h**

I contemplated a ton and came to the eventual realization that I wanted a new robotic arm so as a result, I'm making a massive motor controller. It takes some inspiration from the first design and first setup but this is meant for Nema 23 motors and Nema 17 motors too. Not just 3 nema 17s. It's way bigger. I made a full PCB by myself and ran some checks and fixes with AI and now I'll route it. My friend and I researched a ton and discussed a ton also to come to this schematisc. We worked extremely hard as I really needed a new robotic arm after mine just broke. Additionally, I've been thinking for a while now that I need a bigger and better arm, so as a result this is what I've made. I've also prioritized safety and made sure that it would work. It seems really nice so far. I hope it will be as good as I'm expecting it to be once it's all done. I also added a few cool features on it alongside with the motor controllers. I think you can see for yourself. Budgeting all the parts was also quite a big problem too. I still managed to figure everything out. If this can be accepted, it will be massive for me. I've worked on nema motor control for a few months now and this is my main project, a custom PCB for a completely new robotic arm. This is a huge stepping stone for me. Please accept it as it will be a huge help for me. I also had to work on the power and making sure that the motors wouldn't overheat too. The drivers were the main cost. The parts itself weren't too expensive but the drivers cost a ton.

### 2026-11-08: I routed the whole thing, fixed a few issues, and added a ton of planes to help with the power. I routed it carefully, making sure to make what needed to be thick big and dilligently used the space to

**4h**

I routed the whole thing, fixed a few issues, and added a ton of planes to help with the power. I routed it carefully, making sure to make what needed to be thick big and dilligently used the space to my advangage while keeping it as compact as possible. I made it based off the style of a cnc shield and fully organized it and routed it with a bit of help from AI to fix issues. It looks really nice and I think it's ready to submit.
